{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately BEFORE the current text in the same invented story.","text":"The afternoon before, rain had chased Mara and her mother into the public library.

They had only meant to return a book, but while her mother spoke to the librarian, Mara wandered between the shelves, listening to the storm patter against the tall windows. The children’s section smelled of dust and wet coats. A drop slid down the glass, paused, then raced another drop to the sill.

“Look,” Mara whispered, as if the raindrops might hear her.

At the end of the aisle, a book rested face-out on a low display. Its cover showed a silver cloud floating over a row of small houses. The title was The Secret Weather of Ordinary Days.

Mara pulled it free and opened to the first page. There was a faint pencil mark beside a sentence about listening for changes in the wind. Someone had drawn a tiny star in the margin.

“Found something?” her mother asked.

“I think so.” Mara hugged the book to her chest.

On the way home, the storm had passed, leaving the pavement glossy and the air smelling of leaves. They stopped at Grandma’s house to drop off a jar of soup. Grandma was sitting by the window with her knitting, watching the clouds drift apart.

“Rain can make the world look freshly invented,” she said.

Mara told her about the book. Grandma’s eyes brightened, and she repeated what she often said: weather was never ordinary if you paid close attention.

That evening, Mara read two chapters at the kitchen table, then tucked the book beneath her spelling worksheets so it wouldn’t get bent. Outside, a last rumble moved across the sky, far away."}
